reviewMetadata.sourceLessonFamily: Mathematical Habits, Place Value, and Rounding

learnerMaterial.title: A Digit Has a Place-Value Job
learnerMaterial.subject: mathematics
learnerMaterial.lessonGoal: Today you will compare the value of the same digit in two places. This helps you read, compare, and check large numbers.
successCriteria: I can name the place of a digit.
I can tell when one digit value is 10 times another.
I can explain my answer with place-value words.
keyPoints: A digit's place tells its value.
One place to the left is 10 times as much.
One place to the right is one tenth as much.

vocabulary.definition: one symbol used to write a number, such as 3
the value a digit has because of its place

sections.title: One digit, two jobs
sections.body: The digit 3 can have different values. Look at its place before you compare.

sections.title: Worked example: 3,000 and 300
sections.directions: This is an example. The answer and thinking are shown. You do not type anything here.

items.prompt: How many times as much is the 3 in 3,000 as the 3 in 300?

steps: The thousands place is one place left of the hundreds place.
One place left makes the value 10 times as much.

items.prompt: 4,000 is how many times as much as 400?

feedback.correct: That works. The 4 moved from the hundreds place to the thousands place, so its value became 10 times as much.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the two places. The thousands place is one place left of the hundreds place. Use the one-place rule and try a fresh question.

sections.title: Practice: find the digit's value
sections.directions: Answer each question on your own.

items.prompt: In which number does the digit 6 mean six thousand?

feedback.correct: You matched the 6 to the thousands place.
feedback.incorrect: Find the thousands column first. Then check which number has 6 in that place.

items.prompt: 900 is how many times as much as 90?

feedback.correct: Yes. The 9 is one place farther left in 900.
feedback.incorrect: Compare the hundreds place with the tens place. They are one place apart.

sections.title: Reteach: use a smaller pair
sections.body: Think about 20 and 2. Two tens are 10 times two ones. Now use the same idea with a fresh pair.

items.prompt: 700 is how many times as much as 70?

feedback.correct: You used the same one-place pattern with hundreds and tens.
feedback.incorrect: Point to the 7 in each number. Count how many places it moved, then use the one-place rule.

sections.title: Check what you can explain
sections.directions: Answer without using the worked example.

items.prompt: Compare the 5 in 5,000 with the 5 in 500. Tell how many times as much it is and why.

feedback.correct: Your explanation connects the digit's places to its values. That is place-value reasoning.
feedback.incorrect: Name both places first. Then tell how the value changes when the 5 moves one place left.

whatYouLearned: A digit's place tells its value.
Moving one place left makes a digit's value 10 times as much.
A place-value chart can help you explain the change.
